builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Accelerating LLM Pretraining with Zeroth-Order Curvature on Idle Serving Compute
summary: ZO-Curv replaces the standard AdamW pretraining update with a curvature-adapted first-order update, where curvature is estimated by forward-only zeroth-order queries dispatched to idle inference-serving hardware that would otherwise sit unused. The cost is a heterogeneous training-and-serving orchestration layer, finite-query curvature estimation noise, and the need for serving devices that can run the model's forward pass while a separate training node performs first-order steps. The approach can fail when insufficient idle serving compute is available, when noisy curvature estimates mislead the update at small query budgets, or when the operational complexity of co-scheduling training and serving outweighs the wall-clock gain.
rationale: The method targets LLM pretraining at 125M-1.5B scale and presumes a pool of idle serving hardware plus first-order training infrastructure, which exceeds the reader's single 24 GB GPU and no-pretraining constraint, so it is relevant to track but not actionable.
technique: Zeroth-order curvature estimation on idle serving compute

claims.statement: ZO-Curv replaces the standard AdamW pretraining update with a curvature-adapted first-order update, where curvature is estimated by forward-only zeroth-order queries dispatched to idle inference-serving hardware that would otherwise sit unused. The cost is a heterogeneous training-and-serving orchestration layer, finite-query curvature estimation noise, and the need for serving devices that can run the model's forward pass while a separate training node performs first-order steps. The approach can fail when insufficient idle serving compute is available, when noisy curvature estimates mislead the update at small query budgets, or when the operational complexity of co-scheduling training and serving outweighs the wall-clock gain.
At 770M parameters, reaches AdamW's 20K-step validation loss in 3.9 hours instead of 7.5 hours, with lower final loss of 2.70 versus 2.84 under the same step budget.
